title: Vector Algebra
description: Class 12 IMO — Vector Algebra: vectors and components, magnitude and unit vectors, the dot (scalar) product and the cross (vector) product with their applications.

topics.title: Vectors and Components
topics.concept:
A vector has both magnitude and direction (e.g. displacement, force), unlike a scalar which has magnitude only. In space a vector is written $\vec{a}=a_1\hat{i}+a_2\hat{j}+a_3\hat{k}$.

Magnitude and unit vectors

The magnitude is $|\vec a|=\sqrt{a_1^2+a_2^2+a_3^2}$. A unit vector in the direction of $\vec a$ is $\hat a=\dfrac{\vec a}{|\vec a|}$.

Types of vectors

  • Zero vector $\vec 0$: magnitude $0$, no definite direction.
  • Unit vector: magnitude $1$.
  • Equal vectors: same magnitude and direction.
  • Collinear/parallel: $\vec a=\lambda\vec b$ for some scalar $\lambda$.

Addition and scalar multiplication

Add componentwise; scalar $\lambda$ multiplies each component (triangle/parallelogram law geometrically). The position vector of a point $P(x,y,z)$ is $x\hat i+y\hat j+z\hat k$, and the vector from $A$ to $B$ is $\overrightarrow{AB}=\vec b-\vec a$ (position vector of $B$ minus that of $A$). The section formula gives the point dividing $AB$ in ratio $m:n$ as $\dfrac{m\vec b+n\vec a}{m+n}$.

examples.problem: Find $|\vec a|$ for $\vec a=3\hat i+4\hat k$.
Find the unit vector along $\vec a=2\hat i+3\hat j+6\hat k$.
examples.solution: $|\vec a|=\sqrt{4+9+36}=\sqrt{49}=7$. So $\hat a=\dfrac{1}{7}(2\hat i+3\hat j+6\hat k).$
$\overrightarrow{AB}=\vec b-\vec a=(4-1)\hat i+(6-2)\hat j+(3-3)\hat k=3\hat i+4\hat j.$

examples.problem: Find the midpoint of $A(2,0,4)$ and $B(0,2,0)$ as a position vector.
examples.solution: Midpoint $=\dfrac{\vec a+\vec b}{2}=\dfrac{(2\hat i+4\hat k)+(2\hat j)}{2}=\hat i+\hat j+2\hat k.$

recap: $\overrightarrow{AB}=\vec b-\vec a$; section formula $\dfrac{m\vec b+n\vec a}{m+n}$.

topics.title: Dot (Scalar) Product
topics.concept:
The dot product of two vectors produces a scalar:

$$\vec a\cdot\vec b=|\vec a||\vec b|\cos\theta = a_1b_1+a_2b_2+a_3b_3,$$

where $\theta$ is the angle between them.

Key consequences

  • Angle: $\cos\theta=\dfrac{\vec a\cdot\vec b}{|\vec a||\vec b|}$.
  • Perpendicularity: $\vec a\perp\vec b \iff \vec a\cdot\vec b=0$.
  • $\vec a\cdot\vec a=|\vec a|^2$.
  • Projection of $\vec a$ on $\vec b$: $\dfrac{\vec a\cdot\vec b}{|\vec b|}$.

The dot product is commutative ($\vec a\cdot\vec b=\vec b\cdot\vec a$) and distributive over addition.

examples.problem: Find $\vec a\cdot\vec b$ for $\vec a=\hat i+2\hat j+3\hat k$, $\vec b=2\hat i-\hat j+\hat k$.
Are $\vec a=\hat i+\hat j$ and $\vec b=\hat i-\hat j$ perpendicular?
examples.solution: $\vec a\cdot\vec b=1\cdot1+1\cdot(-1)=0$. Since the dot product is $0$, yes, they are perpendicular.

examples.problem: Find the angle between $\vec a=\hat i$ and $\vec b=\hat i+\hat j$.
Find the projection of $\vec a=2\hat i+3\hat j$ on $\vec b=\hat i$.

recap: $\vec a\perp\vec b \iff \vec a\cdot\vec b=0$; $\ \vec a\cdot\vec a=|\vec a|^2$.
Projection of $\vec a$ on $\vec b$ is $\dfrac{\vec a\cdot\vec b}{|\vec b|}$.

quiz.explanation: A unit vector dotted with itself equals 1.

quiz.q: If θ is the angle between any two vectors a and b, then |a.b| = |a × b| when θ is equal to:
quiz.explanation: |a||b||cosθ| = |a||b||sinθ|. This implies |tanθ| = 1. The angle in the first quadrant is π/4 (45°).

topics.title: Cross (Vector) Product
topics.concept:
The cross product of two vectors produces a vector perpendicular to both:

$$\vec a\times\vec b=|\vec a||\vec b|\sin\theta\,\hat n = \begin{vmatrix}\hat i&\hat j&\hat k\\a_1&a_2&a_3\\b_1&b_2&b_3\end{vmatrix},$$

where $\hat n$ is the unit vector perpendicular to the plane of $\vec a,\vec b$ (right-hand rule).

Key consequences

  • Anti-commutative: $\vec a\times\vec b=-(\vec b\times\vec a)$.
  • Parallel test: $\vec a\parallel\vec b \iff \vec a\times\vec b=\vec 0$.
  • $|\vec a\times\vec b|$ is the area of the parallelogram with sides $\vec a,\vec b$; half of it is the triangle's area.
  • $\sin\theta=\dfrac{|\vec a\times\vec b|}{|\vec a||\vec b|}$.

examples.problem: Find $\vec a\times\vec b$ for $\vec a=\hat i+\hat j$, $\vec b=\hat j+\hat k$.
examples.solution: $\vec a\times\vec b=\begin{vmatrix}\hat i&\hat j&\hat k\\1&1&0\\0&1&1\end{vmatrix}=\hat i(1\cdot1-0\cdot1)-\hat j(1\cdot1-0\cdot0)+\hat k(1\cdot1-1\cdot0)=\hat i-\hat j+\hat k.$

examples.problem: Find the area of the parallelogram with adjacent sides $\vec a=\hat i+\hat j$ and $\vec b=\hat j+\hat k$.
examples.solution: From Example 1, $\vec a\times\vec b=\hat i-\hat j+\hat k$, so area $=|\vec a\times\vec b|=\sqrt{1+1+1}=\sqrt3$ square units.

examples.problem: Are $\vec a=2\hat i+4\hat j$ and $\vec b=\hat i+2\hat j$ parallel?
examples.solution: $\vec a=2\vec b$, so they are parallel. Check: $\vec a\times\vec b=\begin{vmatrix}\hat i&\hat j&\hat k\\2&4&0\\1&2&0\end{vmatrix}=\vec 0$, confirming parallelism.

examples.problem: Find the area of the triangle with sides $\vec a=\hat i+\hat j$, $\vec b=\hat j+\hat k$.

recap: $\vec a\times\vec b$ is a vector $\perp$ both, magnitude $|\vec a||\vec b|\sin\theta$.
$|\vec a\times\vec b|=$ area of parallelogram; triangle area $=\tfrac12|\vec a\times\vec b|$.

Area of the triangle formed by i and j is:
If the vectors a = 2î + λĵ + k̂ and b = î − 2ĵ + 3k̂ are perpendicular to each other, find the value of λ.
questions.explanation: For perpendicular vectors, a.b = 0. So, (2)(1) + (λ)(−2) + (1)(3) = 0 → 2 − 2λ + 3 = 0 → 5 = 2λ → λ = 5/2.

questions.q: Two oxen are pulling a cart in an Indian farm. One pulls with a force F₁ = 10î + 5ĵ N, and the other pulls with F₂ = 5î − 5ĵ N. What is the resultant force on the cart?
questions.explanation: Resultant Force F = F₁ + F₂ = (10î + 5ĵ) + (5î − 5ĵ) = 15î N. The forces in the j direction cancel out.

questions.q: If a × b = a × c and a ≠ 0, then which of the following is definitely true?
questions.explanation: a × b − a × c = 0 → a × (b − c) = 0. This means that either b − c = 0 (so b = c), or vector a is parallel to vector (b − c). Thus, b=c is not 'definitely' true, but a being parallel to (b−c) encompasses the general relationship (including the zero vector case trivially).

If two vectors are collinear, which of the following statements is ALWAYS false?
options: They are scalar multiples of each other.
They must have the same direction.
questions.explanation: Collinear vectors are parallel but can have opposite directions (anti-parallel). Thus, they don't must have the same direction.

options: Area of a triangle with sides a and b
Area of a parallelogram with adjacent sides a and b
questions.explanation: The magnitude of the cross product of two vectors represents the area of a parallelogram whose adjacent sides are given by those vectors.

questions.q: Which of the following is equal to the scalar triple product [b c a]?
questions.explanation: Cyclic permutations of the vectors in a scalar triple product leave its value unchanged. Hence, [b c a] = [a b c].
